no harness-enforced turn refusal (second tier per ticket). - `parseTaskLedger` lives in the loop (`TaskLedgerEvent` → host persist, `Agent.finalizeGate` default off); the ledger is a `custom` record shaped like `model_request_summary`, folded last-wins into `TrajectorySnapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to null, corrupt payloads never break replay). - Declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`; `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended` keyed on the LIVE approval mode) — the create-bucket dead-end class. - Bench telemetry: terminal-bench gains a per-task `checklist` column, harbor a `Checklist coverage` block; both parse the LAST `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` = verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`). - Wire protocol carries `task_ledger` (golden fixture + web client kind list) so external hosts see the ledger too. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/agent test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart test/trajectory/task_ledger_fold_test.dart test/tools/request_secret_tool_test.dart dart test test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart --tags integration # IT-1/IT-2: mock LLM + real bash python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa ``` E2E-1/REG-1 (real-model bench re-runs) stay with the supervised bench harness per the repo's no-live-LLM-in-PR-path rule; the contract is already on for them because both harnesses boot `approvalMode: autopilot`.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
real command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[task-ledger block in final answer] L --> P[TaskLedgerEvent
loop parse] P --> R[hidden task_ledger record] R --> S[snapshot.taskLedger fold] R --> B[bench summary
checklist V/T line] ```

+def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers
+
+
+_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")
+
+
+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:
+        return "checklist: none"
+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []
+    total = len(items)
+    verified = sum(
+        1
+        for item in items
+        if isinstance(item, dict)
+        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
+    )
+    unmet = total - verified
+    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell
+

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. +def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:

+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:

+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)

+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:

+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)

+    if unmet:

+    return cell

+def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers

+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:

+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []

+    unmet = total - verified
+    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell

+def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers
+

+_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")
+

+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:
+        return "checklist: none"
+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []
+    total = len(items)
+    verified = sum(
+        1
+        for item in items
+        if isinstance(item, dict)
+        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
+    )
+    unmet = total - verified
+    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1418 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1418 - **Title**: gh-1412 [GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1412` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 34 - **Additions**: +1885 - **Deletions**: -22 - **Created**: 2026-10-08T14:06:17Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-08T14:19:09Z ## PR Description Closes #1412 ### What changed Unattended fa runs now verify produced state against the task text before declaring done: the system prompt gains the **FinalizeGate** contract (unattended/bench only), the run's final answer is parsed for its `task-ledger` checklist block and persisted as a hidden `task_ledger` session record, and the bench summaries report near-miss proximity from those records. ### Key decisions - Contract rides the prompt only when boot `approvalMode == unattended` (bench harnesses already set `autopilot`) — interactive modes stay byte-identical; no harness-enforced turn refusal (second tier per ticket). - `parseTaskLedger` lives in the loop (`TaskLedgerEvent` → host persist, `Agent.finalizeGate` default off); the ledger is a `custom` record shaped like `model_request_summary`, folded last-wins into `TrajectorySnapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to null, corrupt payloads never break replay). - Declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`; `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended` keyed on the LIVE approval mode) — the create-bucket dead-end class. - Bench telemetry: terminal-bench gains a per-task `checklist` column, harbor a `Checklist coverage` block; both parse the LAST `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` = verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`). - Wire protocol carries `task_ledger` (golden fixture + web client kind list) so external hosts see the ledger too. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/agent test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart test/trajectory/task_ledger_fold_test.dart test/tools/request_secret_tool_test.dart dart test test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart --tags integration # IT-1/IT-2: mock LLM + real bash python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa ``` E2E-1/REG-1 (real-model bench re-runs) stay with the supervised bench harness per the repo's no-live-LLM-in-PR-path rule; the contract is already on for them because both harnesses boot `approvalMode: autopilot`.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
real command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[task-ledger block in final answer] L --> P[TaskLedgerEvent
loop parse] P --> R[hidden task_ledger record] R --> S[snapshot.taskLedger fold] R --> B[bench summary
checklist V/T line] ```

+def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers
+

+_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")

+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:
+        return "checklist: none"
+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []
+    total = len(items)
+    verified = sum(
+        1
+        for item in items
+        if isinstance(item, dict)
+        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
+    )
+    unmet = total - verified
+    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell

Now let me review the key logic issues I can spot so far:

1. **`_lastLedgerBlock` bug candidate**: When `inside` is true and a NEW fence line opens with `task-ledger` info... let's trace: for each fence line, if `inside` → `inside = false` (treats ANY fence line as a closing fence, including one that opens a new task-ledger block). Consider text:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: b
   ```
   First fence: inside=true, last=null. Second fence (` ``` ` closing): inside=false. Third fence (` ```task-ledger `): inside=true, last=null. Fourth fence: inside=false. Body accumulates lines between open and close: when inside and line not fence → `last = last ?? '' + line + '\n'`. Wait, after opening third fence, last=null, then lines accumulate. OK that works.
   
   BUT: there's an asymmetry bug — the loop only sets `last` for lines while `inside`. If a `task-ledger` fence opens and never closes (unterminated), lines still accumulate — test covers that ("unterminated final block still parses").
   
   What about the case where the closing fence line itself carries the task-ledger info? E.g.:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```task-ledger
   ```
   Line 3 is a fence while inside → treated as closing. Content parsed: `- requirement: a`. Fine.
   
   Edge: what if a ledger item contains a line starting with ```? Unlikely.

   Another subtle issue in `_lastLedgerBlock`: nested code blocks. If the final answer quotes a `task-ledger` block inside an outer fenced block... marginal.

   Actually a real edge: the parser scans ALL lines of the final message. If the answer contains a plain ``` fence BEFORE the task-ledger block that never closes... e.g.:
   ```
   ```bash
   test -x script.py
   ```task-ledger      <- this is the opening of ledger, but it's INSIDE the bash fence in the rendered markdown sense
   ```
   The parser doesn't track plain fences; it only treats `task-ledger` info fences as open/close toggles. Any fence line while inside closes. This is a heuristic; acceptable.

2. **`parseTaskLedger` regex issue**: entry regex `^\s*-\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. A continuation field line must start with whitespace: `^\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. But note that the ENTRY regex also matches a line like `  - requirement: x` (indented dash). OK.
   
   However, there's an issue: `field` regex matches ANY indented `key: value` line — including the NEXT item's fields if indentation lost. Fine, heuristic.

   What about multi-line values (a requirement that spans lines)? Not supported; values are single-line. The contract template is single-line. OK.

   **Subtle**: `- requirement: create script.py` where the requirement itself contains `: ` — e.g. `- requirement: note: this`. The regex `([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` — group(1)=`requirement`, group(2)=`note: this`. Fine since `[A-Za-z_]+` stops at the first colon.

   But what if the requirement contains a leading `- ` and the next line begins with `- something: ...`? Standard.

3. **`fromName`**: `'[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` is actually `'$name'`. `.trim().toLowerCase().split(RegExp(r'\s')).first` — if name is empty string, split gives `['']`, first = ''. startsWith('pass') false, startsWith('fix') false → fail. OK. If name is null → 'null' → fail. OK.

   Hmm wait: `'$name'` where name is an Object? — `name.toString()`. For a status of "fixed (chmod applied)" → token = "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" → startsWith('fix') → fixed. Good.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1418 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1418 - **Title**: gh-1412 [GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1412` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 34 - **Additions**: +1885 - **Deletions**: -22 - **Created**: 2026-10-08T14:06:17Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-08T14:19:09Z ## PR Description Closes #1412 ### What changed Unattended fa runs now verify produced state against the task text before declaring done: the system prompt gains the **FinalizeGate** contract (unattended/bench only), the run's final answer is parsed for its `task-ledger` checklist block and persisted as a hidden `task_ledger` session record, and the bench summaries report near-miss proximity from those records. ### Key decisions - Contract rides the prompt only when boot `approvalMode == unattended` (bench harnesses already set `autopilot`) — interactive modes stay byte-identical; no harness-enforced turn refusal (second tier per ticket). - `parseTaskLedger` lives in the loop (`TaskLedgerEvent` → host persist, `Agent.finalizeGate` default off); the ledger is a `custom` record shaped like `model_request_summary`, folded last-wins into `TrajectorySnapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to null, corrupt payloads never break replay). - Declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`; `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended` keyed on the LIVE approval mode) — the create-bucket dead-end class. - Bench telemetry: terminal-bench gains a per-task `checklist` column, harbor a `Checklist coverage` block; both parse the LAST `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` = verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`). - Wire protocol carries `task_ledger` (golden fixture + web client kind list) so external hosts see the ledger too. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/agent test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart test/trajectory/task_ledger_fold_test.dart test/tools/request_secret_tool_test.dart dart test test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart --tags integration # IT-1/IT-2: mock LLM + real bash python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa ``` E2E-1/REG-1 (real-model bench re-runs) stay with the supervised bench harness per the repo's no-live-LLM-in-PR-path rule; the contract is already on for them because both harnesses boot `approvalMode: autopilot`.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
real command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[task-ledger block in final answer] L --> P[TaskLedgerEvent
loop parse] P --> R[hidden task_ledger record] R --> S[snapshot.taskLedger fold] R --> B[bench summary
checklist V/T line] ```

+def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers
+
+
+_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")
+
+
+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:
+        return "checklist: none"
+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []
+    total = len(items)
+    verified = sum(
+        1
+        for item in items
+        if isinstance(item, dict)
+        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
+    )
+    unmet = total - verified
+    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell

Now let me review the key logic issues I can spot so far:

1. **`_lastLedgerBlock` bug candidate**: When `inside` is true and a NEW fence line opens with `task-ledger` info... let's trace: for each fence line, if `inside` → `inside = false` (treats ANY fence line as a closing fence, including one that opens a new task-ledger block). Consider text:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: b
   ```
   First fence: inside=true, last=null. Second fence (` ``` ` closing): inside=false. Third fence (` ```task-ledger `): inside=true, last=null. Fourth fence: inside=false. Body accumulates lines between open and close: when inside and line not fence → `last = last ?? '' + line + '\n'`. Wait, after opening third fence, last=null, then lines accumulate. OK that works.
   
   BUT: there's an asymmetry bug — the loop only sets `last` for lines while `inside`. If a `task-ledger` fence opens and never closes (unterminated), lines still accumulate — test covers that ("unterminated final block still parses").
   
   What about the case where the closing fence line itself carries the task-ledger info? E.g.:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```task-ledger
   ```
   Line 3 is a fence while inside → treated as closing. Content parsed: `- requirement: a`. Fine.
   
   Edge: what if a ledger item contains a line starting with ```? Unlikely.

   Another subtle issue in `_lastLedgerBlock`: nested code blocks. If the final answer quotes a `task-ledger` block inside an outer fenced block... marginal.

   Actually a real edge: the parser scans ALL lines of the final message. If the answer contains a plain ``` fence BEFORE the task-ledger block that never closes... e.g.:
   ```
   ```bash
   test -x script.py
   ```task-ledger      <- this is the opening of ledger, but it's INSIDE the bash fence in the rendered markdown sense
   ```
   The parser doesn't track plain fences; it only treats `task-ledger` info fences as open/close toggles. Any fence line while inside closes. This is a heuristic; acceptable.

2. **`parseTaskLedger` regex issue**: entry regex `^\s*-\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. A continuation field line must start with whitespace: `^\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. But note that the ENTRY regex also matches a line like `  - requirement: x` (indented dash). OK.
   
   However, there's an issue: `field` regex matches ANY indented `key: value` line — including the NEXT item's fields if indentation lost. Fine, heuristic.

   What about multi-line values (a requirement that spans lines)? Not supported; values are single-line. The contract template is single-line. OK.

   **Subtle**: `- requirement: create script.py` where the requirement itself contains `: ` — e.g. `- requirement: note: this`. The regex `([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` — group(1)=`requirement`, group(2)=`note: this`. Fine since `[A-Za-z_]+` stops at the first colon.

   But what if the requirement contains a leading `- ` and the next line begins with `- something: ...`? Standard.

3. **`fromName`**: `'[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` is actually `'$name'`. `.trim().toLowerCase().split(RegExp(r'\s')).first` — if name is empty string, split gives `['']`, first = ''. startsWith('pass') false, startsWith('fix') false → fail. OK. If name is null → 'null' → fail. OK.

   Hmm wait: `'$name'` where name is an Object? — `name.toString()`. For a status of "fixed (chmod applied)" → token = "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" → startsWith('fix') → fixed. Good.

4. **`TaskLedger.fromJson`**: `[for (final row in raw) ?TaskLedgerItem.fromJson(row)]` — null-aware element. Good.

5. **The `verified` getter**: `status != fail` → pass and fixed verified. Good.

6. **Duplicated Python code**: `_ledger_records` and `_ledger_cell` are copy-pasted verbatim between `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` and `bench/terminal_bench/summary.py` (≈60 lines duplicated). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION). Given the two bench harnesses are separate dirs with separate test suites, maybe deliberate. There's precedent? Let me check if bench harnesses share code elsewhere.

7. **`render` in harbor summary**: `fully = sum(1 for _, cell in ledgered if " unmet" not in cell)` — a ledger with 0 items ("checklist: 0/0") would count as fully verified without " unmet". Edge: ledger with empty items list → cell "checklist: 0/0" → counts as fully verified. Dart side never persists an empty ledger (fromJson returns null if items empty; parseTaskLedger returns null). But a malformed/foreign record could have data.items = []. Minor.

8. **harbor `_ledger_records` scans `agent*/fah-sessions`** but the terminal_bench test writes `agent-logs/fah-sessions` and the harbor test writes `agent/fah-sessions`. In terminal_bench summary.py, `_ledger_records` globs `agent*/fah-sessions` too. OK — matches `agent-logs` too since `agent*` matches `agent-logs`. Good.

9. **Terminal-bench `checklist_facts` keyed by trial_name**: `checklist_facts = {trial: _ledger_cell(trial_dir) for trial, trial_dir in _trial_dirs(runs_dir).items()}` then `checklist_facts.get(r.get("trial_name", "?"), "checklist: none")`. Need to check `_trial_dirs` to verify keys are trial names. Let me read summary.py fully.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1418 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1418 - **Title**: gh-1412 [GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1412` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 34 - **Additions**: +1885 - **Deletions**: -22 - **Created**: 2026-10-08T14:06:17Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-08T14:19:09Z ## PR Description Closes #1412 ### What changed Unattended fa runs now verify produced state against the task text before declaring done: the system prompt gains the **FinalizeGate** contract (unattended/bench only), the run's final answer is parsed for its `task-ledger` checklist block and persisted as a hidden `task_ledger` session record, and the bench summaries report near-miss proximity from those records. ### Key decisions - Contract rides the prompt only when boot `approvalMode == unattended` (bench harnesses already set `autopilot`) — interactive modes stay byte-identical; no harness-enforced turn refusal (second tier per ticket). - `parseTaskLedger` lives in the loop (`TaskLedgerEvent` → host persist, `Agent.finalizeGate` default off); the ledger is a `custom` record shaped like `model_request_summary`, folded last-wins into `TrajectorySnapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to null, corrupt payloads never break replay). - Declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`; `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended` keyed on the LIVE approval mode) — the create-bucket dead-end class. - Bench telemetry: terminal-bench gains a per-task `checklist` column, harbor a `Checklist coverage` block; both parse the LAST `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` = verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`). - Wire protocol carries `task_ledger` (golden fixture + web client kind list) so external hosts see the ledger too. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/agent test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart test/trajectory/task_ledger_fold_test.dart test/tools/request_secret_tool_test.dart dart test test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart --tags integration # IT-1/IT-2: mock LLM + real bash python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa ``` E2E-1/REG-1 (real-model bench re-runs) stay with the supervised bench harness per the repo's no-live-LLM-in-PR-path rule; the contract is already on for them because both harnesses boot `approvalMode: autopilot`.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
real command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[task-ledger block in final answer] L --> P[TaskLedgerEvent
loop parse] P --> R[hidden task_ledger record] R --> S[snapshot.taskLedger fold] R --> B[bench summary
checklist V/T line] ```

+def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers
+

+_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")
+

+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:
+        return "checklist: none"
+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []
+    total = len(items)
+    verified = sum(
+        1
+        for item in items
+        if isinstance(item, dict)
+        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
+    )
+    unmet = total - verified
+    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell

1. **`_lastLedgerBlock` bug candidate**: When `inside` is true and a NEW fence line opens with `task-ledger` info... let's trace: for each fence line, if `inside` → `inside = false` (treats ANY fence line as a closing fence, including one that opens a new task-ledger block). Consider text:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: b
   ```
   First fence: inside=true, last=null. Second fence (` ``` ` closing): inside=false. Third fence (` ```task-ledger `): inside=true, last=null. Fourth fence: inside=false. Body accumulates lines between open and close: when inside and line not fence → `last = last ?? '' + line + '\n'`. Wait, after opening third fence, last=null, then lines accumulate. OK that works.
   
   BUT: there's an asymmetry bug — the loop only sets `last` for lines while `inside`. If a `task-ledger` fence opens and never closes (unterminated), lines still accumulate — test covers that ("unterminated final block still parses").
   
   What about the case where the closing fence line itself carries the task-ledger info? E.g.:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```task-ledger
   ```
   Line 3 is a fence while inside → treated as closing. Content parsed: `- requirement: a`. Fine.
   
   Edge: what if a ledger item contains a line starting with ```? Unlikely.

   Another subtle issue in `_lastLedgerBlock`: nested code blocks. If the final answer quotes a `task-ledger` block inside an outer fenced block... marginal.

   Actually a real edge: the parser scans ALL lines of the final message. If the answer contains a plain ``` fence BEFORE the task-ledger block that never closes... e.g.:
   ```
   ```bash
   test -x script.py
   ```task-ledger      <- this is the opening of ledger, but it's INSIDE the bash fence in the rendered markdown sense
   ```
   The parser doesn't track plain fences; it only treats `task-ledger` info fences as open/close toggles. Any fence line while inside closes. This is a heuristic; acceptable.

2. **`parseTaskLedger` regex issue**: entry regex `^\s*-\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. A continuation field line must start with whitespace: `^\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. But note that the ENTRY regex also matches a line like `  - requirement: x` (indented dash). OK.
   
   However, there's an issue: `field` regex matches ANY indented `key: value` line — including the NEXT item's fields if indentation lost. Fine, heuristic.

   What about multi-line values (a requirement that spans lines)? Not supported; values are single-line. The contract template is single-line. OK.

   **Subtle**: `- requirement: create script.py` where the requirement itself contains `: ` — e.g. `- requirement: note: this`. The regex `([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` — group(1)=`requirement`, group(2)=`note: this`. Fine since `[A-Za-z_]+` stops at the first colon.

   But what if the requirement contains a leading `- ` and the next line begins with `- something: ...`? Standard.

3. **`fromName`**: `'[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` is actually `'$name'`. `.trim().toLowerCase().split(RegExp(r'\s')).first` — if name is empty string, split gives `['']`, first = ''. startsWith('pass') false, startsWith('fix') false → fail. OK. If name is null → 'null' → fail. OK.

   Hmm wait: `'$name'` where name is an Object? — `name.toString()`. For a status of "fixed (chmod applied)" → token = "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" → startsWith('fix') → fixed. Good.

4. **`TaskLedger.fromJson`**: `[for (final row in raw) ?TaskLedgerItem.fromJson(row)]` — null-aware element. Good.

5. **The `verified` getter**: `status != fail` → pass and fixed verified. Good.

6. **Duplicated Python code**: `_ledger_records` and `_ledger_cell` are copy-pasted verbatim between `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` and `bench/terminal_bench/summary.py` (≈60 lines duplicated). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION). Given the two bench harnesses are separate dirs with separate test suites, maybe deliberate. There's precedent? Let me check if bench harnesses share code elsewhere.

7. **`render` in harbor summary**: `fully = sum(1 for _, cell in ledgered if " unmet" not in cell)` — a ledger with 0 items ("checklist: 0/0") would count as fully verified without " unmet". Edge: ledger with empty items list → cell "checklist: 0/0" → counts as fully verified. Dart side never persists an empty ledger (fromJson returns null if items empty; parseTaskLedger returns null). But a malformed/foreign record could have data.items = []. Minor.

8. **harbor `_ledger_records` scans `agent*/fah-sessions`** but the terminal_bench test writes `agent-logs/fah-sessions` and the harbor test writes `agent/fah-sessions`. In terminal_bench summary.py, `_ledger_records` globs `agent*/fah-sessions` too. OK — matches `agent-logs` too since `agent*` matches `agent-logs`. Good.

9. **Terminal-bench `checklist_facts` keyed by trial_name**: `checklist_facts = {trial: _ledger_cell(trial_dir) for trial, trial_dir in _trial_dirs(runs_dir).items()}` then `checklist_facts.get(r.get("trial_name", "?"), "checklist: none")`. Need to check `_trial_dirs` to verify keys are trial names. Let me read summary.py fully.

10. **`agent.dart` `finalizeGate` mutable field**: The PR description says hosts flip it right after the stack lands. `Agent.finalizeGate` is read at `_runAgentLoop` config construction time? Let me check: in agent.dart the loop config is built per run with `finalizeGate: finalizeGate` — reading the field at run start. The CLI sets `_agent.finalizeGate = ...` right after stack creation. But the doc says "keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval mode" for `isUnattended` — that's the request_secret path. For finalizeGate, it's boot-time only (the prompt composition is also boot-time). The AGENTS.md blurb says the `/approval` switch flips `isUnattended` but the FinalizeGate contract is boot-time (explicitly documented in `_withFinalizeGate` doc comment: "an interactive `/approval` switch never recomposes the contract"). But hold on — the prompt uses `config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended` while `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended` also boot-time. Consistent.

    Wait, there's an inconsistency worth checking: `agent_cli_prompt.dart` doc says "bench and headless runs set `approvalMode: autopilot`" but the code checks `ApprovalMode.unattended`. Are `autopilot` and `unattended` the same enum value? The PR description says "boot `approvalMode == unattended` (bench harnesses already set `autopilot`)". Let me check the ApprovalMode enum — maybe `autopilot` is an alias for `unattended`. Need to verify.

11. **`isUnattended` closure**: `() => _approval.mode == ApprovalMode.unattended` — live check. Good.

12. **`_onTaskLedger` in trajectory_commands.dart**: persists after every TaskLedgerEvent. The event fires once per run. Fine. Error → printed to TUI, never thrown. Good. But `io.writeln(tuiError(...))` — check tuiError exists there.

14. **Wire protocol**: `_decodeTaskLedger` throws FormatException when ledger has no items — consistent with the "LOUD malformed frame" pattern. Encoding `{'ledger': ledger.toJson()}`. Golden fixture added. Web client kind list updated. Good.

    But note the golden fixture file `test/wire/fixtures/v1/events/task_ledger.json` has no trailing newline ("\ No newline at end of file"). Check other fixtures — do they have trailing newlines? Minor.

15. **The odd whitespace-only change in agent_loop.dart `_errorToolResult`**: reindentation of a string continuation (dart format artifact). Harmless but unrelated churn — worth a SUGGESTION? It's formatting noise; fine.

16. **trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart**: also contains an unrelated reindent of `SegmentPinRecord()` switch case (`'${record.pinned...}'`) — dart format churn. Note.

17. **Test in test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart**: `apiKey: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` is actually `apiKey: 'test-key'` or similar (redacted in my view). Fine.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. +def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)

+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"

Now let me review the key logic issues I can spot so far:

1. **`_lastLedgerBlock` bug candidate**: When `inside` is true and a NEW fence line opens with `task-ledger` info... let's trace: for each fence line, if `inside` → `inside = false` (treats ANY fence line as a closing fence, including one that opens a new task-ledger block). Consider text:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: b
   ```
   First fence: inside=true, last=null. Second fence (` ``` ` closing): inside=false. Third fence (` ```task-ledger `): inside=true, last=null. Fourth fence: inside=false. Body accumulates lines between open and close: when inside and line not fence → `last = last ?? '' + line + '\n'`. Wait, after opening third fence, last=null, then lines accumulate. OK that works.
   
   BUT: there's an asymmetry bug — the loop only sets `last` for lines while `inside`. If a `task-ledger` fence opens and never closes (unterminated), lines still accumulate — test covers that ("unterminated final block still parses").
   
   What about the case where the closing fence line itself carries the task-ledger info? E.g.:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```task-ledger
   ```
   Line 3 is a fence while inside → treated as closing. Content parsed: `- requirement: a`. Fine.
   
   Edge: what if a ledger item contains a line starting with ```? Unlikely.

   Another subtle issue in `_lastLedgerBlock`: nested code blocks. If the final answer quotes a `task-ledger` block inside an outer fenced block... marginal.

   Actually a real edge: the parser scans ALL lines of the final message. If the answer contains a plain ``` fence BEFORE the task-ledger block that never closes... e.g.:
   ```
   ```bash
   test -x script.py
   ```task-ledger      <- this is the opening of ledger, but it's INSIDE the bash fence in the rendered markdown sense
   ```
   The parser doesn't track plain fences; it only treats `task-ledger` info fences as open/close toggles. Any fence line while inside closes. This is a heuristic; acceptable.

2. **`parseTaskLedger` regex issue**: entry regex `^\s*-\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. A continuation field line must start with whitespace: `^\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. But note that the ENTRY regex also matches a line like `  - requirement: x` (indented dash). OK.
   
   However, there's an issue: `field` regex matches ANY indented `key: value` line — including the NEXT item's fields if indentation lost. Fine, heuristic.

   What about multi-line values (a requirement that spans lines)? Not supported; values are single-line. The contract template is single-line. OK.

   **Subtle**: `- requirement: create script.py` where the requirement itself contains `: ` — e.g. `- requirement: note: this`. The regex `([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` — group(1)=`requirement`, group(2)=`note: this`. Fine since `[A-Za-z_]+` stops at the first colon.

   But what if the requirement contains a leading `- ` and the next line begins with `- something: ...`? Standard.

3. **`fromName`**: `'[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` is actually `'$name'`. `.trim().toLowerCase().split(RegExp(r'\s')).first` — if name is empty string, split gives `['']`, first = ''. startsWith('pass') false, startsWith('fix') false → fail. OK. If name is null → 'null' → fail. OK.

   Hmm wait: `'$name'` where name is an Object? — `name.toString()`. For a status of "fixed (chmod applied)" → token = "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" → startsWith('fix') → fixed. Good.

4. **`TaskLedger.fromJson`**: `[for (final row in raw) ?TaskLedgerItem.fromJson(row)]` — null-aware element. Good.

5. **The `verified` getter**: `status != fail` → pass and fixed verified. Good.

6. **Duplicated Python code**: `_ledger_records` and `_ledger_cell` are copy-pasted verbatim between `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` and `bench/terminal_bench/summary.py` (≈60 lines duplicated). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION). Given the two bench harnesses are separate dirs with separate test suites, maybe deliberate. There's precedent? Let me check if bench harnesses share code elsewhere.

7. **`render` in harbor summary**: `fully = sum(1 for _, cell in ledgered if " unmet" not in cell)` — a ledger with 0 items ("checklist: 0/0") would count as fully verified without " unmet". Edge: ledger with empty items list → cell "checklist: 0/0" → counts as fully verified. Dart side never persists an empty ledger (fromJson returns null if items empty; parseTaskLedger returns null). But a malformed/foreign record could have data.items = []. Minor.

8. **harbor `_ledger_records` scans `agent*/fah-sessions`** but the terminal_bench test writes `agent-logs/fah-sessions` and the harbor test writes `agent/fah-sessions`. In terminal_bench summary.py, `_ledger_records` globs `agent*/fah-sessions` too. OK — matches `agent-logs` too since `agent*` matches `agent-logs`. Good.

9. **Terminal-bench `checklist_facts` keyed by trial_name**: `checklist_facts = {trial: _ledger_cell(trial_dir) for trial, trial_dir in _trial_dirs(runs_dir).items()}` then `checklist_facts.get(r.get("trial_name", "?"), "checklist: none")`. Need to check `_trial_dirs` to verify keys are trial names. Let me read summary.py fully.

10. **`agent.dart` `finalizeGate` mutable field**: The PR description says hosts flip it right after the stack lands. `Agent.finalizeGate` is read at `_runAgentLoop` config construction time? Let me check: in agent.dart the loop config is built per run with `finalizeGate: finalizeGate` — reading the field at run start. The CLI sets `_agent.finalizeGate = ...` right after stack creation. But the doc says "keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval mode" for `isUnattended` — that's the request_secret path. For finalizeGate, it's boot-time only (the prompt composition is also boot-time). no harness-enforced turn refusal (second tier per ticket). - `parseTaskLedger` lives in the loop (`TaskLedgerEvent` → host persist, `Agent.finalizeGate` default off); the ledger is a `custom` record shaped like `model_request_summary`, folded last-wins into `TrajectorySnapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to null, corrupt payloads never break replay). - Declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`; `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended` keyed on the LIVE approval mode) — the create-bucket dead-end class. - Bench telemetry: terminal-bench gains a per-task `checklist` column, harbor a `Checklist coverage` block; both parse the LAST `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` = verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`). - Wire protocol carries `task_ledger` (golden fixture + web client kind list) so external hosts see the ledger too. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/agent test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart test/trajectory/task_ledger_fold_test.dart test/tools/request_secret_tool_test.dart dart test test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart --tags integration # IT-1/IT-2: mock LLM + real bash python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa ``` E2E-1/REG-1 (real-model bench re-runs) stay with the supervised bench harness per the repo's no-live-LLM-in-PR-path rule; the contract is already on for them because both harnesses boot `approvalMode: autopilot`.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
real command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[task-ledger block in final answer] L --> P[TaskLedgerEvent
loop parse] P --> R[hidden task_ledger record] R --> S[snapshot.taskLedger fold] R --> B[bench summary
checklist V/T line] ```

+def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers
+
+
+_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")
+
+
+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:
+        return "checklist: none"
+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []
+    total = len(items)
+    verified = sum(
+        1
+        for item in items
+        if isinstance(item, dict)
+        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
+    )
+    unmet = total - verified
+    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell
+

Body accumulates lines between open and close: when inside and line not fence → `last = last ?? '' + line + '\n'`. Wait, after opening third fence, last=null, then lines accumulate. OK that works.
   
   BUT: there's an asymmetry bug — the loop only sets `last` for lines while `inside`. If a `task-ledger` fence opens and never closes (unterminated), lines still accumulate — test covers that ("unterminated final block still parses").
   
   What about the case where the closing fence line itself carries the task-ledger info? E.g.:
   ```
   ```task-ledger

   ```task-ledger
   ```
   Line 3 is a fence while inside → treated as closing. Content parsed: `- requirement: a`. Fine.

def _trial_dirs(runs_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """trial_name -> trial dir, from the same layout _session_facts uses."""
    dirs = {}
    for pattern in ("*/*/*/agent-logs", "*/*/*/agent", "*/*/*/fa-agent-timeout.json"):
        for path in glob.glob(str(runs_dir / pattern)):
            trial_dir = Path(path).parent
            dirs[trial_dir.name] = trial_dir
    return dirs

So the redaction pipeline is attached as tool hooks: `beforeToolCall` redacts tool INPUT (commands going out?) and `afterToolCall` redacts tool RESULT content before it enters context. So the model's context should only contain redacted tool outputs. The model's own final answer text (and thus the ledger) is composed from redacted context — but nothing re-redacts model output. Model output could still contain secrets it was seeded via the user prompt (task text) — e.g. the task text itself may embed credentials ("the token is in the env var FOO" — not a secret). More realistically: the model could echo a secret from... hmm, its training? Not a real vector. The main vector: tool output was redacted before entering context, so the model shouldn't be able to quote secrets it never saw. BUT the `command` field — `beforeToolCall` redacts the command before it's executed? If beforeToolCall redacts tool input, then a command like `grep -q ghp_xxx ~/.git-credentials` would be redacted before execution (making the check fail?) — not my concern.

Still, the repo's own gh-1054 review convention explicitly says free-text fields persisted into session records must pass through the redaction pipeline ("the session JSONL is an audit surface and must not leak secrets the in-run hooks already mask elsewhere"). `_onTaskLedger` skips that. Even if defense-in-depth, it's a deviation from an established security convention introduced exactly for this class of record (`custom` records with free-text fields). I'd rate it **IMPORTANT** (defense-in-depth violation of an established convention) rather than BLOCKING — since the in-run hooks already mask secrets before the model sees them, the practical leak path is narrow (e.g., redaction disabled by config — `config.redactionPipeline` nullable; in bench runs is it on?). +def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers
+
+
+_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")
+
+
+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:
+        return "checklist: none"
+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []
+    total = len(items)
+    verified = sum(
+        1
+        for item in items
+        if isinstance(item, dict)
+        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
+    )
+    unmet = total - verified
+    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1418 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1418 - **Title**: gh-1412 [GOAL] Near-miss elimination: FinalizeGate contract + TaskLedger — the agent verifies produced state against task text before declaring done - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1412` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 34 - **Additions**: +1885 - **Deletions**: -22 - **Created**: 2026-10-08T14:06:17Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-08T14:19:09Z ## PR Description Closes #1412 ### What changed Unattended fa runs now verify produced state against the task text before declaring done: the system prompt gains the **FinalizeGate** contract (unattended/bench only), the run's final answer is parsed for its `task-ledger` checklist block and persisted as a hidden `task_ledger` session record, and the bench summaries report near-miss proximity from those records. ### Key decisions - Contract rides the prompt only when boot `approvalMode == unattended` (bench harnesses already set `autopilot`) — interactive modes stay byte-identical; no harness-enforced turn refusal (second tier per ticket). - `parseTaskLedger` lives in the loop (`TaskLedgerEvent` → host persist, `Agent.finalizeGate` default off); the ledger is a `custom` record shaped like `model_request_summary`, folded last-wins into `TrajectorySnapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to null, corrupt payloads never break replay). - Declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`; `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended` keyed on the LIVE approval mode) — the create-bucket dead-end class. - Bench telemetry: terminal-bench gains a per-task `checklist` column, harbor a `Checklist coverage` block; both parse the LAST `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` = verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`). - Wire protocol carries `task_ledger` (golden fixture + web client kind list) so external hosts see the ledger too. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/agent test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart test/trajectory/task_ledger_fold_test.dart test/tools/request_secret_tool_test.dart dart test test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart --tags integration # IT-1/IT-2: mock LLM + real bash python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa ``` E2E-1/REG-1 (real-model bench re-runs) stay with the supervised bench harness per the repo's no-live-LLM-in-PR-path rule; the contract is already on for them because both harnesses boot `approvalMode: autopilot`.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR T[task text] --> CL[checklist extraction
agent-authored] CL --> V{verify each item
real command vs state} V -->|fail| FIX[fix + re-verify] V -->|pass| L[task-ledger block in final answer] L --> P[TaskLedgerEvent
loop parse] P --> R[hidden task_ledger record] R --> S[snapshot.taskLedger fold] R --> B[bench summary
checklist V/T line] ```

+def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
+    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
+    session logs, in file then line order."""
+    ledgers = []
+    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
+        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
+            try:
+                text = path.read_text()
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            for line in text.splitlines():
+                line = line.strip()
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    record = json.loads(line)
+                except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    isinstance(record, dict)
+                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
+                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
+                ):
+                    ledgers.append(record)
+    return ledgers

+def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
+    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
+    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
+    when the session carries no ledger."""
+    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
+    if not ledgers:
+        return "checklist: none"
+    items = ((ledgers[-1].get("data") or {}).get("items")) or []
+    total = len(items)

+    if unmet:
+        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
+    return cell

blocks.text:
Now let me review the key logic issues I can spot so far:

1. **`_lastLedgerBlock` bug candidate**: When `inside` is true and a NEW fence line opens with `task-ledger` info... let's trace: for each fence line, if `inside` → `inside = false` (treats ANY fence line as a closing fence, including one that opens a new task-ledger block). Consider text:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: b
   ```
   First fence: inside=true, last=null. Second fence (` ``` ` closing): inside=false. Third fence (` ```task-ledger `): inside=true, last=null. Fourth fence: inside=false. Body accumulates lines between open and close: when inside and line not fence → `last = last ?? '' + line + '\n'`. Wait, after opening third fence, last=null, then lines accumulate. OK that works.
   
   BUT: there's an asymmetry bug — the loop only sets `last` for lines while `inside`. If a `task-ledger` fence opens and never closes (unterminated), lines still accumulate — test covers that ("unterminated final block still parses").
   
   What about the case where the closing fence line itself carries the task-ledger info? E.g.:
   ```
   ```task-ledger
   - requirement: a
   ```task-ledger
   ```
   Line 3 is a fence while inside → treated as closing. Content parsed: `- requirement: a`. Fine.
   
   Edge: what if a ledger item contains a line starting with ```? Unlikely.

   Another subtle issue in `_lastLedgerBlock`: nested code blocks. If the final answer quotes a `task-ledger` block inside an outer fenced block... marginal.

   Actually a real edge: the parser scans ALL lines of the final message. If the answer contains a plain ``` fence BEFORE the task-ledger block that never closes... e.g.:
   ```
   ```bash
   test -x script.py
   ```task-ledger      <- this is the opening of ledger, but it's INSIDE the bash fence in the rendered markdown sense
   ```
   The parser doesn't track plain fences; it only treats `task-ledger` info fences as open/close toggles. Any fence line while inside closes. This is a heuristic; acceptable.

2. **`parseTaskLedger` regex issue**: entry regex `^\s*-\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. A continuation field line must start with whitespace: `^\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$`. But note that the ENTRY regex also matches a line like `  - requirement: x` (indented dash). OK.
   
   However, there's an issue: `field` regex matches ANY indented `key: value` line — including the NEXT item's fields if indentation lost. Fine, heuristic.

   What about multi-line values (a requirement that spans lines)? Not supported; values are single-line. The contract template is single-line. OK.

   **Subtle**: `- requirement: create script.py` where the requirement itself contains `: ` — e.g. `- requirement: note: this`. The regex `([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` — group(1)=`requirement`, group(2)=`note: this`. Fine since `[A-Za-z_]+` stops at the first colon.

   But what if the requirement contains a leading `- ` and the next line begins with `- something: ...`? Standard.

3. **`fromName`**: `'[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` is actually `'$name'`. `.trim().toLowerCase().split(RegExp(r'\s')).first` — if name is empty string, split gives `['']`, first = ''. startsWith('pass') false, startsWith('fix') false → fail. OK. If name is null → 'null' → fail. OK.

   Hmm wait: `'$name'` where name is an Object? — `name.toString()`. For a status of "fixed (chmod applied)" → token = "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" → startsWith('fix') → fixed. Good.

4. **`TaskLedger.fromJson`**: `[for (final row in raw) ?TaskLedgerItem.fromJson(row)]` — null-aware element. Good.

5. **The `verified` getter**: `status != fail` → pass and fixed verified. Good.

6. **Duplicated Python code**: `_ledger_records` and `_ledger_cell` are copy-pasted verbatim between `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` and `bench/terminal_bench/summary.py` (≈60 lines duplicated). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION). Given the two bench harnesses are separate dirs with separate test suites, maybe deliberate. There's precedent? Let me check if bench harnesses share code elsewhere.

7. **`render` in harbor summary**: `fully = sum(1 for _, cell in ledgered if " unmet" not in cell)` — a ledger with 0 items ("checklist: 0/0") would count as fully verified without " unmet". Edge: ledger with empty items list → cell "checklist: 0/0" → counts as fully verified. Dart side never persists an empty ledger (fromJson returns null if items empty; parseTaskLedger returns null). But a malformed/foreign record could have data.items = []. Minor.

8. **harbor `_ledger_records` scans `agent*/fah-sessions`** but the terminal_bench test writes `agent-logs/fah-sessions` and the harbor test writes `agent/fah-sessions`. In terminal_bench summary.py, `_ledger_records` globs `agent*/fah-sessions` too. OK — matches `agent-logs` too since `agent*` matches `agent-logs`. Good.

9. **Terminal-bench `checklist_facts` keyed by trial_name**: `checklist_facts = {trial: _ledger_cell(trial_dir) for trial, trial_dir in _trial_dirs(runs_dir).items()}` then `checklist_facts.get(r.get("trial_name", "?"), "checklist: none")`. Need to check `_trial_dirs` to verify keys are trial names. Let me read summary.py fully.

10. **`agent.dart` `finalizeGate` mutable field**: The PR description says hosts flip it right after the stack lands. `Agent.finalizeGate` is read at `_runAgentLoop` config construction time? Let me check: in agent.dart the loop config is built per run with `finalizeGate: finalizeGate` — reading the field at run start. The CLI sets `_agent.finalizeGate = ...` right after stack creation. But the doc says "keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval mode" for `isUnattended` — that's the request_secret path. For finalizeGate, it's boot-time only (the prompt composition is also boot-time). The AGENTS.md blurb says the `/approval` switch flips `isUnattended` but the FinalizeGate contract is boot-time (explicitly documented in `_withFinalizeGate` doc comment: "an interactive `/approval` switch never recomposes the contract"). But hold on — the prompt uses `config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended` while `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended` also boot-time. Consistent.

    Wait, there's an inconsistency worth checking: `agent_cli_prompt.dart` doc says "bench and headless runs set `approvalMode: autopilot`" but the code checks `ApprovalMode.unattended`. Are `autopilot` and `unattended` the same enum value? The PR description says "boot `approvalMode == unattended` (bench harnesses already set `autopilot`)". Let me check the ApprovalMode enum — maybe `autopilot` is an alias for `unattended`. Need to verify.

11. **`isUnattended` closure**: `() => _approval.mode == ApprovalMode.unattended` — live check. Good.

12. **`_onTaskLedger` in trajectory_commands.dart**: persists after every TaskLedgerEvent. The event fires once per run. Fine. Error → printed to TUI, never thrown. Good. But `io.writeln(tuiError(...))` — check tuiError exists there.

13. **`agent_event_handler.dart`**: added `onTaskLedger` param — check that all callers updated (approval_commands.dart updated). Any other callers? Let me grep.

14. **Wire protocol**: `_decodeTaskLedger` throws FormatException when ledger has no items — consistent with the "LOUD malformed frame" pattern. Encoding `{'ledger': ledger.toJson()}`. Golden fixture added. Web client kind list updated. Good.

    But note the golden fixture file `test/wire/fixtures/v1/events/task_ledger.json` has no trailing newline ("\ No newline at end of file"). Check other fixtures — do they have trailing newlines? Minor.

15. **The odd whitespace-only change in agent_loop.dart `_errorToolResult`**: reindentation of a string continuation (dart format artifact). Harmless but unrelated churn — worth a SUGGESTION? It's formatting noise; fine.

16. **trajectory_snapshot_builder.dart**: also contains an unrelated reindent of `SegmentPinRecord()` switch case (`'${record.pinned...}'`) — dart format churn. Note.

17. **Test in test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart**: `apiKey: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` is actually `apiKey: 'test-key'` or similar (redacted in my view). Fine.
